name: Medill-Northwestern Journalism Institute (Medill Cherubs)
org: Northwestern University Medill School of Journalism
summary: The Medill Cherubs program is a prestigious five-week summer institute for rising high school seniors interested in journalism, media, and storytelling. Students learn print, digital, broadcast, photo, and audio journalism from seasoned industry professionals and Medill faculty, completing reporting assignments across the Chicago area.
eligibility: High school juniors (rising seniors) with strong writing skills and a interest in journalism.
cost: Tuition covers room, board, and course materials; financial aid is available.

name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
summary: An immersive summer research internship program offering high school and college students hands-on experience in NIH intramural laboratories. Interns work side-by-side with leading scientists across biomedical research, computational biology, biostatistics, and behavioral sciences.
eligibility: High school seniors (17+ years of age at program start or living within 40 miles of campus if 17) who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
cost: Paid monthly stipend provided

name: Microsoft Discovery Program
summary: A 4-week paid summer internship designed for graduating high school seniors who are passionate about technology. Interns work in small teams on real projects for Microsoft product teams, learn core programming concepts, and receive structured mentorship from Microsoft employees.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors living near Redmond, WA or Atlanta, GA with completed pre-calculus or equivalent coursework.
cost: Paid internship

name: Medical School HQ eShadowing
summary: eShadowing provides free, weekly live and recorded virtual clinical shadowing sessions hosted by physicians and physician assistants. High school and pre-health students participate in case presentations, Q&A sessions, and weekly quizzes to earn verifiable certificates documenting clinical shadowing hours.
eligibility: Open to high school and pre-health students interested in medicine or healthcare careers
cost: Free live sessions and attendance tracking with optional quiz completion for certificates

name: EnergyMag High School Virtual Internship
summary: EnergyMag offers a year-round remote internship for high school students interested in renewable energy, clean tech, and technology analysis. Interns work remotely with a dedicated mentor to research specific companies, technologies, or clean energy markets, producing a publishable report and receiving a letter of accomplishment upon completion.
eligibility: High school sophomores, juniors, and seniors interested in renewable energy and research
cost: Free remote internship

name: Girls Who Code Pathways Program
summary: The Pathways Program is a free, self-paced virtual summer program designed for female and non-binary high school students. Participants build independent coding projects across specialized tracks—including Data Science & AI, Web Development, Game Design, and Cybersecurity—with live advisory support and networking events.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) who identify as female, trans, or non-binary
cost: Free self-paced program

name: Medicine Encompassed Student Member Internship
summary: Medicine Encompassed is a student-run nonprofit offering remote flexible roles in medical writing, editing, graphic design, and curriculum creation. Interns work in teams to produce educational resources across 18 medical specialty committees and publish articles, promoting healthcare literacy for underserved youth.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) globally interested in STEAM, biology, and healthcare
cost: Free unpaid remote role with flexible time commitment (1-2 hours per week)

name: Youth as Solutions
summary: A guided year-long service-learning program where teams of middle and high school students collaborate with adult mentors to solve local challenges. Student teams select focus areas such as education, civics and democracy, community health, or the environment, receiving $250–$1,000 in project implementation grants, monthly leadership coaching, and national networking opportunities.
eligibility: Teams of at least 2 youth in grades 6-12 paired with an adult mentor.
cost: Free (Provides $250-$1,000 project seed grants)

name: American Red Cross Youth Volunteer Leadership
summary: A structured national volunteer program that empowers high school students to lead community health initiatives, blood drives, disaster preparedness training, and peer safety workshops through local Red Cross Youth Clubs and councils. High school volunteers undergo formal training in leadership, emergency response, and public health project management while completing measurable service projects.
eligibility: High school students located in the United States.
cost: Free

name: Sigma Xi Student Research Showcase
org: Sigma Xi, The Scientific Research Honor Society
summary: The Sigma Xi Student Research Showcase is an annual virtual science communication competition and conference for high school, undergraduate, and graduate students. Participants build a dedicated website featuring a research abstract, technical slideshow, and a short video explaining their findings to a general audience. Judges evaluate submissions across 13 STEM disciplines and award monetary prizes for top presentations.
eligibility: High school, undergraduate, and graduate students worldwide conducting original STEM research.
cost: $35 for members, $50 for non-members

name: AISES National Conference Student Research Competition
org: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
summary: The AISES National Conference features a dedicated Student Research Competition celebrating pre-college through graduate students who combine Indigenous knowledge with scientific innovation. High school participants present oral or poster presentations in STEM categories to peers, mentors, and professional scientists. Presenters receive constructive feedback and opportunities for registration discounts or awards.
eligibility: Middle school through graduate students conducting STEM research, with an emphasis on Indigenous and native student researchers.
cost: Registration fee applies; free or discounted for early abstract submitters

name: United States Senate Youth Program
org: United States Senate & The Hearst Foundations
summary: The United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP) brings high school student leaders from every state to Washington, D.C., for an intensive week-long study of the federal government. Selected delegates meet with senators, Supreme Court justices, and federal agency leadership, and each delegate receives a $10,000 undergraduate college scholarship.
eligibility: High school juniors or seniors serving in an elected or appointed student leadership position who are U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents.
cost: Fully funded all-expenses-paid trip to Washington, D.C., plus a $10,000 undergraduate scholarship

name: Plan International USA Youth Advisory Board
summary: The Youth Advisory Board (YAB) at Plan International USA gives youth leaders aged 14 to 22 a platform to shape international development and domestic gender equity initiatives. Members advise executive leadership, participate in national advocacy campaigns, and help lead youth engagement projects.
eligibility: U.S. residents aged 14 to 22 interested in gender equality, global issues, and youth-led advocacy.
cost: Free to participate; travel and lodging expenses for in-person retreats are fully funded

name: UC Berkeley Business Academy for Youth (B-BAY)
org: UC Berkeley Haas School of Business
summary: The UC Berkeley Business Academy for Youth (B-BAY) offers summer residency programs and founder bootcamps for high school students. Guided by Berkeley Haas faculty and corporate guest speakers, students learn business fundamentals, conduct market research, develop detailed business plans, and pitch startup ideas.
eligibility: High school students interested in business, leadership, and startup ventures.
cost: Paid program tuition; financial aid and scholarships available

name: NYU High School Summer Art Intensive
summary: A 4-week studio art program in New York City where high school students explore digital art, painting, and sculpture under NYU Steinhardt faculty. Participants visit NYC contemporary art galleries and museums, develop advanced artistic technique, and compile a strong portfolio for college admissions.
eligibility: High school students currently in 9th, 10th, or 11th grade with demonstrated interest in studio arts; requires portfolio submission of 10-15 works.
cost: Tuition fee applies; need-based scholarships are available

name: Interlochen Arts Camp High School Division
summary: A renowned multi-week summer conservatory experience in northern Michigan offering rigorous creative training across visual arts, music, creative writing, film and animation, theatre, and dance. High school students learn from professional faculty, participate in intensive studio work, and prepare portfolios or performance auditions.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 through 12 interested in fine arts, music, creative writing, or performing arts.
cost: Tuition varies by program length (1 to 6 weeks); financial aid and merit scholarships available

name: The Cooper Union Summer Art Intensive
summary: A 4-week pre-college program in Manhattan offering specialized concentrations in drawing, animation, painting, graphic design, and studio practice. Taught by professional artists and Cooper Union alumni, students experience personal studio space, rigorous critique culture, and targeted portfolio preparation.
eligibility: High school students aged 15-18 who are rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors.
cost: $4,350 tuition including materials; full merit scholarships available for NYC public high school students

name: Brown HealthCORE Program
org: Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University
summary: HealthCORE is a two-week summer pre-med pathway program hosted by Brown University's Warren Alpert Medical School to expose high school students to medical professions. Participants attend daily clinical lectures, engage in interactive anatomy lab sessions, and practice vital signs and clinical assessment skills with mock patients. The initiative aims to build foundational clinical knowledge and support early interest in medicine.
eligibility: High school students interested in healthcare careers, with preference given to local/regional applicants.
cost: Fully funded community pipeline program

name: HackTJ
org: Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology
summary: HackTJ is a 24-hour student-run high school hackathon where participants form small teams to build software applications, web platforms, AI tools, or hardware prototypes. Attendees gain access to mentorship from software engineers, tech workshops, and sponsor challenges. The event concludes with project judging and awards across multiple technical categories.
eligibility: Current high school students; no prior computer science or coding experience required.
cost: Free for accepted high school participants

name: NextGen Bootcamp Computer Science Summer Certificate Program
summary: NextGen Bootcamp offers intensive computer science and programming summer bootcamps held in-person in NYC as well as live online. High school students learn fundamental to advanced concepts in Python, Java, data science, machine learning, and web development. Courses emphasize hands-on project building and real-world application creation under expert guidance.
eligibility: High school students and gap year students aged 13-18.
cost: Varies by course track and format

name: Georgia Tech CEISMC Summer PEAKS High School Sessions
summary: CEISMC Summer PEAKS at Georgia Tech offers one- to two-week experiential summer sessions on campus in Atlanta for high schoolers. Courses dive into advanced topics across engineering, robotics, electrical circuits, and computer science. Students participate in hands-on design challenges, lab work, and interactive projects led by Georgia Tech faculty and staff.
eligibility: Rising 9th through 12th grade students.
cost: $400–$550 per weekly session; need-based scholarships available

name: Non-Trivial Fellowship
summary: The Non-Trivial Fellowship is a fully funded remote program that helps young people aged 14–20 conduct research and start projects addressing humanity's most pressing challenges, with a major focus on AI safety, alignment, and risk governance. Fellows receive expert mentorship, join a global peer network, and work on substantial research papers or technical projects. Top projects receive scholarships and grants ranging from $500 up to $10,000.
eligibility: Aged 14–20 and have not yet started university
cost: Fully free; offers project grants and scholarships from $500 to $10,000

name: Supervised Program for Alignment Research (SPAR)
summary: SPAR (Supervised Program for Alignment Research) is a remote, part-time research program connecting high school and undergraduate students with experienced AI safety researchers. Mentees commit 5–20 hours per week over 3 months to work on structured technical alignment or AI governance research projects. Projects frequently result in open-source codebases, research write-ups, or submissions to top machine learning conferences.
eligibility: Open to anyone 13 or older, including high school students with a background or interest in Python, CS, or AI policy
cost: Free volunteer research mentorship program

name: Stanford AI4ALL
summary: Stanford AI4ALL is a selective summer program hosted by Stanford University aimed at introducing high school students to artificial intelligence with a focus on ethical design and social impact. Participants learn core machine learning concepts, hear lectures from leading Stanford scholars, and collaborate in small teams on research projects tackling issues in healthcare, climate, or algorithmic fairness. The curriculum emphasizes responsible AI development and diversifying the future tech workforce.
eligibility: Rising 10th, 11th, or 12th graders residing in the U.S. or Puerto Rico, with priority for students underrepresented in AI
cost: $4,000 tuition; need-based financial aid is available for eligible families

name: Dilemmas and Dangers in AI Course
summary: Leaf offers free online introductory courses for ambitious high school students, including its specialized 'Dilemmas and Dangers in AI' track. The course covers frontier AI safety concepts, catastrophic risk mitigation, technical alignment dilemmas, and global AI governance through curated readings and weekly group discussions led by experienced facilitators. Graduates gain access to Leaf's alumni network, project incubation funding, and direct pathways to research fellowships.
eligibility: High school students aged 14–18 worldwide
cost: Fully free

name: Veritas AI Fellowship
summary: The Veritas AI Fellowship is an intensive 12- to 15-week virtual research program where high school students build independent AI projects under 1-on-1 mentorship from graduate researchers at top universities like Harvard and MIT. Students explore advanced machine learning concepts, data science, and AI ethics while creating an original research paper or software artifact. The program includes guidance on publishing research in high school or peer-reviewed journals.
eligibility: High school students with prior coding experience in Python or completion of the Veritas AI Scholars course
cost: $5,400 for AI Fellowship; need-based financial aid available for introductory AI Scholars prerequisite

name: Summer Program on Applied Rationality and Cognition (SPARC)
summary: SPARC is a selective, free residential summer program designed for high school students looking to improve their mental habits and quantitative decision-making under uncertainty. The curriculum combines decision theory, probability, game theory, cognitive science, and AI literacy to help students build self-agency and rigorous critical thinking skills. Participants engage in interactive workshops, Fermi estimations, and student-led collaborative projects.
eligibility: High school students globally with strong quantitative, logical, and analytical reasoning skills.
cost: Free tuition, room, and board, with travel stipends available for students in need

name: European Summer Program in Rationality (ESPR)
summary: ESPR is an immersive 10-day residential summer workshop for mathematically minded high school students aged 16 to 19. The curriculum focuses on developing a toolbox of quantitative reasoning skills through subjects such as game theory, mathematical logic, decision theory, cognitive science, and AI safety evaluation. Outside of seminars, participants lead their own intellectual discussions and collaborative activities.
eligibility: Students aged 16 to 19 globally interested in quantitative thinking and rationality.
cost: Free tuition, room, and board, with travel scholarships available

name: Reason & Rationality High School Foundation Program
summary: Reason & Rationality is a selective residential summer program hosted at university sites like Princeton that teaches critical thinking through structured, small-group intellectual salons. Guided by PhD instructors from institutions like Harvard and Princeton, students analyze 20 core concepts across philosophy, public policy, game theory, and economics. The program focuses on teaching teens how to evaluate arguments, model incentives, and engage in civil, truth-seeking debate.
eligibility: Students entering 9th grade through recent high school graduates.
cost: Tuition-based residential program with 1-week and 2-week options

name: High School Sustainable Energy Education (SEE) Program
org: Johns Hopkins University Ralph O'Connor Sustainable Energy Institute (ROSEI)
summary: The High School Sustainable Energy Education (SEE) program is a four-week intensive summer course co-developed by ROSEI and Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation. Students learn fundamental engineering and science concepts behind renewable energy technologies, including hydroelectric, solar, wind, and biomass, while exploring real-world solutions for climate change and sustainable energy systems.
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering, renewable energy, and climate solutions.
cost: Tuition required (financial aid available through Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation)

name: Biomedical Research and Global Health Program
org: Seattle Children's Research Institute & Highline Public Schools
summary: This year-long academic program immerses high school students in biomedical research and global health topics in a professional laboratory setting. Students learn core laboratory safety and analytical skills, use advanced lab equipment, analyze case studies on disease prevention and elimination, and hear directly from leading scientific researchers.
eligibility: Open to 11th and 12th grade students in Highline, Federal Way, Tukwila, and Tahoma school districts in Washington state; prior biology coursework recommended.
cost: Free academic credit program provided via school district partnership

name: Inspire STEM Clean Energy Summer Program
summary: The Inspire STEM Youth Workforce Development Program is a 6-week summer internship designed for high school juniors and seniors interested in clean energy careers. Participants gain hands-on exposure to real-world projects, site visits with clean energy corporations, technical skills training, and direct mentorship from industry professionals.
eligibility: Rising high school juniors and seniors from Environmental Justice communities in Boston and surrounding areas.
cost: Free paid summer internship program

name: Columbia Climate School Pre-College Programs
summary: Columbia Climate School offers pre-college workshops and summer intensives that educate high school students on climate change, sustainability, and environmental justice. Guided by Columbia University climate researchers and faculty, students participate in real-time discussions, project-based research learning, and practical problem-solving around planetary health.
eligibility: Open to high school students in grades 9 through 12, including rising 9th graders.
cost: Tuition fees apply depending on program format (online workshops vs. summer intensives)

name: London International Youth Science Forum (LIYSF)
org: London International Youth Science Forum CIC
summary: Hosted at Imperial College London and the Royal Geographical Society, LIYSF is a 15-day residential STEM program for young scientists aged 16–21 from over 90 countries. Participants attend lectures from world-leading scientists and Nobel Laureates, visit top UK research laboratories (including Oxford and Cambridge), and engage in scientific debates and cultural exchanges.
eligibility: Students aged 16–21 with a strong interest in STEM and proficiency in English
cost: £3,295 including 14 nights of central London accommodation, all meals, university/lab visits, and social activities

name: XLAB International Science Camp
summary: Held at Göttingen University in Germany, the XLAB International Science Camp is a 3-week immersive hands-on STEM training program. High school students and young adults work directly alongside university scientists in state-of-the-art research laboratories across physics, chemistry, biology, and computer science.
eligibility: Students aged 17 and older with a strong STEM background and B2 English proficiency
cost: €3,900 covering tuition, room accommodation, and daily meals

name: ISSOS International Summer School
summary: Hosted at historic UK university towns such as St Andrews and Cambridge, ISSOS is a 3-week residential summer program for students aged 13–18 from over 80 countries. Participants pair one core academic subject (such as Business, Creative Writing, Debate, or IB Preparation) with an elective (such as Golf, Leadership, or Photography) alongside cultural excursions.
eligibility: Students aged 13–18 worldwide (maximum 10% representation per nationality)
cost: All-inclusive tuition, accommodation, meals, electives, and cultural trips (varies by campus location)

name: J.W. Patterson Tournament of Champions
summary: The J.W. Patterson Tournament of Champions (TOC) is widely considered the premier national championship for high school speech and debate circuit debaters, hosted every April by the University of Kentucky. High school competitors earn entry by securing qualification 'bids' at major national tournaments throughout the academic year across events such as Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, Congressional Debate, World Schools, and speech events. Winning or placing at the TOC represents one of the highest honors in high school forensics.
eligibility: High school debaters and speakers who earn designated bid qualifications on the national speech and debate circuit.
cost: Entry fees vary by event division (e.g. ~$175 per entry), plus judging and travel fees.

name: Ronald Reagan Great Communicator Debate Series
summary: The Ronald Reagan Great Communicator Debate Series is a national high school debate competition designed to develop proactive, informed, and articulate student leaders. Emulating the civility, humor, storytelling, and persuasion of presidential debates, students compete in regional qualifying tournaments for a spot in the National Championship at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library in California. National finalists compete for a share of $50,000 in college scholarships, with all travel expenses covered for national qualifiers.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 residing in the United States.
cost: Free entry for participants; all-expenses-paid trip to California for national finalists.

name: Harvard National Speech and Debate Tournament
summary: The Harvard National Speech and Debate Tournament is one of the nation's largest and most prestigious high school forensics competitions, hosted every February over Presidents' Day Weekend in Cambridge, MA. Organized by the Harvard Debate Council, the tournament hosts Varsity, Junior Varsity, and Novice divisions across Policy, Lincoln-Douglas, Public Forum, World Schools, Congressional Debate, and various individual speech categories. Thousands of high school debaters from across the country and around the world attend each year.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12; divisions are available for beginner through advanced debaters.
cost: Registration fees apply per entry and event format.

name: picoCTF
summary: picoCTF is a free, game-based cybersecurity competition created by computer security experts at Carnegie Mellon University for middle and high school students. Participants learn real-world ethical hacking, reverse engineering, cryptography, web exploitation, and digital forensics skills through engaging CTF challenges. The annual competition runs online in the spring, while the picoGym platform provides year-round practice.
eligibility: Open to middle school, high school, and college students worldwide.
cost: Free to participate

name: National Cyber League (NCL)
summary: The National Cyber League is a biannual cybersecurity competition for high school and college students designed to bridge the gap between education and real-world careers. Participants solve performance-based challenges in categories like web application penetration testing, network traffic analysis, cryptography, scanning, and forensics. Every participant receives a personalized NCL Scouting Report mapping their skills directly to the NIST NICE Cybersecurity Workforce Framework.
eligibility: High school and college students in the United States.
cost: Free for registered high school teams or $25–$35 per player

name: Lockheed Martin CYBERQUEST
summary: CYBERQUEST is an annual high school cybersecurity competition hosted by Lockheed Martin engineers across multiple regional sites and virtually. Teams of students spend three hours solving multi-step cybersecurity problems in a cloud-based Capture the Flag format. Challenges cover reverse engineering, web exploits, OS security, cryptography, and open-source intelligence.
eligibility: High school students globally in regions hosting CYBERQUEST sites or virtual access.
cost: Free to compete

name: US Cyber Open
summary: The US Cyber Open is an annual national cybersecurity competition and training event designed to identify and mentor emerging cyber athletes. Participants can compete in entry-level or advanced Capture the Flag (CTF) events, attend technical workshops during Cyber Rush Week, and learn red/blue team techniques. Top high school performers can qualify for the US Cyber Team draft to represent the nation in international competitions.
eligibility: High school and college students in the US; US citizenship required for US Cyber Team qualification.
cost: Free registration and participation

name: US Cyber Challenge: Cyber Quests & Cyber Camps
summary: US Cyber Challenge hosts Cyber Quests, a series of online cybersecurity competitions testing participants on packet capture analysis, log forensics, vulnerability assessment, and web security. Top-scoring high school and college competitors receive invitations to weeklong USCC Cyber Camps featuring specialized instruction from SANS Institute instructors, a job fair with defense and tech employers, and a concluding CTF competition.
eligibility: High school, undergraduate, and graduate students in the United States.
cost: Free to participate

name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
summary: The Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program is an 8-week paid summer internship for high school students interested in fisheries, oceanography, and environmental science. Participants are matched with a professional mentor in their local area to conduct field research, participate in habitat restoration, collect samples, and analyze aquatic data. The program aims to increase diversity in fisheries science while offering hands-on conservation experience and a $3,000 stipend.
eligibility: Rising high school juniors, seniors, or rising college freshmen in the U.S., Canada, or Mexico who are at least 16 years old.
cost: Free to participate; provides a $3,000 stipend to students.

name: Salish Sea Sciences Pre-College Program
summary: Salish Sea Sciences offers immersive summer residential programs based in San Juan Island, Washington, focused on marine biology, ecology, and environmental research. Working in collaboration with the University of Washington's Friday Harbor Laboratories, students conduct hands-on field sampling on research vessels, learn scientific methodologies, and participate in ecological restoration projects. Programs range from two to four weeks and provide direct mentorship from professional marine scientists and conservationists.
eligibility: High school students aged 14–18 with an interest in marine and environmental sciences.
cost: $4,900 for 2-week course or $7,400 for 4-week course; financial assistance available.

name: The Institute Discovering Environmental Scientists (TIDES)
org: Hudson River National Estuarine Research Reserve & NYSDEC
summary: The Institute Discovering Environmental Scientists (TIDES) is a two-week paid summer field research and laboratory science experience at the Norrie Point Environmental Center in New York. High school students collaborate with New York State Department of Environmental Conservation scientists and educators to collect real environmental data along the Hudson River estuary. Participants formulate research questions, analyze water quality and fish biological diversity, and present their scientific findings to the local community.
eligibility: High school students residing in the Mid-Hudson Valley, NY area.
cost: Free to participate; provides a stipend and transportation support.

name: UC Davis Young Scholars Program
summary: The UC Davis Young Scholars Program is a six-week residential summer research experience for high school students interested in biological, agricultural, and environmental sciences. Participants live on the UC Davis campus and engage in individual research projects guided by university faculty and research staff in laboratories and outdoor field sites. Program areas include ecology, conservation biology, environmental toxicology, and agricultural sustainability, culminating in a written scientific paper and symposium presentation.
eligibility: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
cost: Program tuition covers housing, meals, field trips, and 5 units of UC credit; substantial financial aid available based on need.

name: Polyphony Lit Student Editorial Staff
summary: A global online platform where high school students edit and publish an international literary magazine. Student editors evaluate submissions of poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, providing detailed, constructive feedback to young authors worldwide.
eligibility: High school students aged 14-18 worldwide
cost: Free to join editorial staff; optional editing workshops available

name: The Adroit Journal Summer Mentorship Program
summary: A six-week online mentorship program that pairs high school writers with established authors and poets for one-on-one drafting, redrafting, and editing guidance. Mentees focus on poetry, fiction, or creative nonfiction, exchanging weekly or biweekly work and building portfolio-ready pieces.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 and gap year students worldwide
cost: $575 tuition; need-based financial aid and fee waivers available

name: ACLU National Advocacy Institute: Washington D.C.
summary: The ACLU National Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C. is an intensive 10-day summer program for high school students focused on issue advocacy, legal strategy, and public policy decision-making. Participants engage directly with ACLU lawyers, lobbyists, and community activists to gain practical tools for civil rights advocacy. The program includes interactive workshops, lectures, site visits across D.C., and collaborative policy discussions.
eligibility: High school students aged 15 to 18 at the time of the program.
cost: Tuition-based program on a college campus; financial aid and full scholarships are available based on need.

name: APAPA National Internship Program
org: Asian Pacific Islander American Public Affairs
summary: A nationwide civic leadership internship placing high school and college students directly into the legislative offices of elected officials and government agencies. Interns gain practical exposure to state and local policy development, legislative tracking, and constituent public service over 8 to 10 weeks. The program combines office placements with professional development seminars and policy workshops.
eligibility: High school and college students located near active APAPA local chapters.
cost: Free to participate; provides a stipend to help cover student expenses.

name: Clinical Neuroscience Immersion Experience (CNI-X)
org: Stanford University Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
summary: CNI-X is an intensive two-week summer program introducing high school students to research and practice across neuroscience, psychiatry, and psychology. Participants attend interactive seminars led by Stanford faculty and collaborate in small teams to complete a capstone project addressing key societal mental health or brain science challenges.
eligibility: Rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors
cost: Tuition required; financial aid/scholarships available

name: Johns Hopkins Internship in Brain Sciences (JHIBS)
org: Johns Hopkins University Department of Neuroscience
summary: JHIBS is an 8-week summer research internship designed to train high school students in brain science and neurological research. Interns engage in hands-on academic research projects in JHU laboratories under faculty mentorship and attend professional development sessions.
eligibility: High school sophomores and juniors with a strong interest in neuroscience and medicine
cost: Free / StiPended

name: UCLA NeuroCamp
summary: NeuroCamp is a free, selective two-week summer program offered by UCLA's Brain Research Institute for Los Angeles-area high schoolers. Students explore fundamental concepts in molecular neurobiology, neuroanatomy, and electrophysiology through faculty lectures, brain dissections, and hands-on laboratory exercises.
eligibility: High school students in the Los Angeles area
cost: Free

name: Humanities and Cognitive Sciences High School Summer Institute (HumCog)
org: The Ohio State University Center for Cognitive and Brain Sciences
summary: HumCog is a week-long summer institute hosted by OSU where high school students explore questions at the intersection of human cognition and the arts. Participants engage in morning lectures with university faculty and afternoon laboratory demonstrations, group discussions, and research activities.
eligibility: Rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors staying within driving distance of OSU campus
cost: Tuition required; partial/full scholarships available

name: Social Justice Research Academy
summary: The Social Justice Research Academy at UPenn is a three-week residential summer program where high school students explore historical and contemporary social movements, inequality, and public policy through sociological frameworks. Participants engage in college-level seminars led by faculty and graduate researchers, conduct field study in Philadelphia, and complete a capstone social research project.
eligibility: Open to rising sophomores, juniors, and seniors globally
cost: $9,700 tuition and residential fees; need-based financial aid is available

name: Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage Internship
summary: The Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage offers internships for high school and university students interested in cultural anthropology, folklore, ethnomusicology, and community studies. Interns conduct qualitative research, assist with cultural sustainability projects, and help produce public cultural programs.
eligibility: Open to high school students, undergraduates, and graduate students
cost: Free to participate; select positions offer stipends

name: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis High School Research Intern
summary: A paid academic-year research internship for high school students passionate about economics and quantitative analysis. Interns work 6 to 10 hours per week under the direct mentorship of a research economist, conducting statistical analysis, literature reviews, data entry, and economic research. Participants also attend internal Research Department seminars.
eligibility: Current high school students who have completed or are enrolled in economics coursework and live within commuting distance of Minneapolis, MN.
cost: Paid position ($17/hour)

name: High School Fed Challenge
org: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
summary: An academic economics research competition hosted by the Federal Reserve System. High school teams act as monetary policy analysts and economists by researching a specific annual economic theme and submitting original academic papers. Top submissions selected by Federal Reserve economists are published in the Journal of Future Economists.
eligibility: U.S. high school students in grades 9-12 competing in teams sponsored by a faculty advisor.
cost: Free to enter and participate

name: KPMG U.S. Empower High School Experience
summary: A 3-week paid summer internship program that introduces high school students to accounting, financial auditing, tax, and advisory services. Interns interact with KPMG professionals and mentors, complete practical business assignments, and explore career pathways in public accounting and professional services.
eligibility: High school students interested in business, finance, or accounting (often recruited through educational partners such as NAF).
cost: Paid internship program

name: Bank of America Financial Center Internship Program
summary: A 7-to-8-week paid summer internship where high school seniors serve as digital ambassadors in Bank of America financial centers. Interns assist clients with mobile banking technology, gain direct exposure to financial services operations, and receive formal financial literacy and professional development training.
eligibility: High school seniors (aged 16+) recruited through partner youth workforce organizations (e.g., Urban Alliance, Boys & Girls Clubs, PYN).
cost: Paid internship position ($17-$24/hour depending on market)

name: Essentials of Finance - Wharton Global Youth Program
summary: An intensive 2-week summer academic program on campus at the Wharton School that introduces students to fundamental concepts in corporate finance, investing, financial markets, and accounting. Participants analyze financial statements, explore valuation techniques, and work on corporate finance case studies alongside Wharton faculty and peers.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-11 with a minimum 3.3 unweighted GPA; prior background in economics or business is helpful.
cost: Tuition costs $7,300 to $12,000 depending on residential or commuter options; need-based financial aid is available

name: Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition
summary: The National High School Design Competition challenges students across the United States to solve real-world community problems using human-centered design principles and creative problem-solving. Participants analyze user needs, iterate on product and interface ideas, and present original prototypes to a panel of expert judges and leading designers. Finalists receive mentorship from professional designers and national recognition.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9–12 or homeschooled equivalents residing in the United States.
cost: Free to enter

name: Wharton Product Design Academy
summary: The Wharton Product Design Academy is an intensive pre-college summer program introducing high school students to the complete design thinking process. Working in teams inside Penn's Studios@Venture Labs, participants conduct user research, reframe complex problems, create testable prototypes, and explore business strategies to launch new products. The experience culminates in a keystone team showcase.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9–11 at the time of application with strong academic performance.
cost: Tuition-based; need-based financial aid available through Wharton Global Youth

name: UCLA Design Media Arts Summer Institute
org: UCLA Department of Design Media Arts
summary: The UCLA Design Media Arts Summer Institute offers high school students rigorous hands-on instruction in digital design, visual media, and interactive art. Taught by UCLA faculty, the curriculum explores 2D typography and graphic design, net art, 3D worldbuilding, and video production. Participants earn college credit while creating portfolio-ready work for creative college applications.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9–12 interested in graphic design, web art, and digital media.
cost: Tuition fees apply; residential, commuter, and virtual options available

name: NextGen Bootcamp UX & UI Design Summer Program
summary: This hands-on summer bootcamp teaches high schoolers essential user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) design skills using Figma. Students create user personas, map user journeys, and construct clickable interactive prototypes for web and mobile applications without needing prior coding knowledge. By the end of the course, participants produce polished digital product designs suitable for a design portfolio.
eligibility: Open to high school students in grades 9–12 interested in app design, web design, and digital UX/UI.
cost: Tuition ranges from $1,299 to $1,699 depending on live online or NYC in-person enrollment

name: TeenArch Studio
summary: TeenArch Studio is a three-week intensive architecture summer experience hosted by UCLA Architecture and Urban Design. High school participants explore architectural concepts, digital rendering, CAD modeling, and design thinking while completing studio projects for university credit. The course provides portfolio pieces suitable for college application to design programs.
eligibility: High school students ages 15 and older with an interest in architecture and urban design.
cost: Approximately $4,245 including course materials and UC college credit

name: Center for Architecture High School Summer Studios
summary: The Center for Architecture offers week-long summer design studio workshops in New York City tailored for high school students. Topics range from architectural sketching and digital bridge design to urban infrastructure and 3D architectural modeling. Guided by practicing architects and educators, students work on site investigations, physical models, and portfolio projects.
eligibility: Open to high school students interested in architecture, drawing, and digital spatial design.
cost: Varies by week and session module

name: Student Design Challenge
summary: The Texas Society of Architects Student Design Challenge invites middle and high school students to submit design solutions for real-world built environment problems. Competitors address annual design briefs focused on community gathering spaces, sustainable architecture, and local infrastructure. Honorees and finalists are celebrated at the annual TxA Conference & Design Expo.
eligibility: Students in grades 6–12 interested in architecture, community design, and spatial planning.
cost: Free to enter

name: Design Discovery Youth
summary: Design Discovery Youth is a summer program organized by Harvard's Graduate School of Design for high school students to explore spatial design fields. Taught by advanced Harvard GSD graduate students, the curriculum introduces participants to architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning. Students engage in drawing, spatial modeling, site analysis, and studio critique.
eligibility: Greater Boston area high school students interested in learning about design and built environments.
cost: Free for accepted local high school students

name: FIT Precollege High School Programs
summary: FIT offers 4-day workshops and 10-day courses designed for high school students interested in fashion design, merchandising, styling, and fashion business. Taught by industry professionals on FIT's NYC campus as well as virtually, these courses allow students to build competitive portfolio pieces, learn hands-on technical skills, and explore diverse careers across the fashion industry.
eligibility: High school students entering grades 9 through 12; beginner-friendly with no portfolio review required.
cost: 4-day workshops start around $440; 10-day courses around $550

name: Parsons Summer Intensive Studies NYC
summary: Parsons Summer Intensive Studies is a 3-week, 3-credit immersive pre-college program in Greenwich Village, NYC. High school students work directly with Parsons faculty on studio projects, fashion design concepts, and portfolio development while participating in field trips and engaging with NYC fashion industry speakers.
eligibility: High school students entering junior or senior year (ages 16–18) and recent high school graduates.
cost: $9,999 total tuition and fees

name: Parsons Paris Online Pre-College Program
summary: Parsons Paris offers asynchronous online fashion courses designed for high school students wanting to explore fashion design and business. Courses such as Inside the Business of Fashion & Luxury and Inside Fashion Design feature video lectures from industry experts, virtual visits to couture workshops, and one-on-one mentor guidance.
eligibility: Open to students ages 13 and older globally year-round.
cost: $1,895 per course

name: Discover Fashion Design at Drexel
summary: Discover Fashion Design at Drexel is an intensive one-week residential summer program at Drexel's Philadelphia campus. High schoolers learn hands-on fashion illustration, draping, natural dyeing, and 3D digital design tools while creating original fashion portfolio pieces and visiting local Philadelphia design studios.
eligibility: High school students who have completed their sophomore year by July and are at least 16 years old.
cost: $2,400 including tuition, accommodations, meals, and field trips

name: Junk Kouture Sustainable Fashion Competition
summary: Junk Kouture is a global sustainable fashion competition challenging middle and high school students to design, upcycle, and model high-end couture garments made entirely from 100% recycled materials. Participants submit design portfolios and performance videos for regional finals, with top teams advancing to national and international runway finals.
eligibility: Open to post-primary/high school students ages 12 to 19 worldwide.
cost: Free to enter

name: American Ballet Theatre Summer Intensive
summary: The American Ballet Theatre Summer Intensive provides advanced classical ballet training grounded in ABT's National Training Curriculum. High school dancers attend daily classes in ballet technique, pointe, repertory, character, and modern dance taught by ABT faculty and guest artists, culminating in a final showcase performance.
eligibility: Dancers ages 12–20 with significant classical ballet background; admission determined via audition.
cost: $4,350 tuition for the 5-week New York program; merit scholarships available

name: Juilliard Summer Dance Intensive
summary: Juilliard's Summer Dance Intensive is a three-week conservatory experience designed for high school dancers pursuing professional goals in dance. Dancers take technique classes in ballet and modern dance, collaborate with guest choreographers, and receive one-on-one advising from Juilliard Dance Division leadership.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-11 at the time of application who have completed at least 1 year of high school and have not yet graduated; audition video required.
cost: $2,400 tuition plus $2,100 room and board; need-based financial aid available

name: The Ailey School Professional Division Summer Intensive
summary: The Ailey School Professional Division Summer Intensive offers five weeks of rigorous modern, contemporary, and ballet dance training in New York City. Students take daily technique classes, learn Ailey repertory, and work with acclaimed choreographers to deepen artistic performance quality.
eligibility: Dancers ages 16–25 with a minimum of 3 years of consistent ballet and modern training; in-person or video audition required.
cost: Tuition ranges from $2,509 to $2,994 depending on division and payment timing; merit scholarships and housing aid available

name: Joffrey Ballet School NYC Hip Hop Summer Intensive
summary: This three-week intensive immerses dancers in urban, commercial, and street dance styles in New York City. Participants take daily classes in breaking, house, locking, jazz/funk, freestyle, and commercial hip-hop, participate in dance battles, and perform in weekly choreographed showcases.
eligibility: Dancers ages 10–25; audition required for acceptance.
cost: Paid program tuition; housing options and scholarships available through audition tour

name: UNCSA Summer Dance Choreographic Institute
org: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
summary: The UNCSA Summer Dance Choreographic Institute is a four-week residency focused on cultivating original composition and choreographic skills in young dancers. Students engage in technique classes, dancemaking workshops, lectures, and creative development under the guidance of UNCSA faculty and visiting choreographers.
eligibility: High school dancers and pre-professionals demonstrating commitment to dance and composition; application/audition required.
cost: Paid tuition with on-campus housing available; financial aid available

name: Culinary Institute of America High School Summer Program
org: Culinary Institute of America & Summer Discovery
summary: The Culinary Institute of America offers an intensive pre-college summer program in Hyde Park, New York, in partnership with Summer Discovery. High school students train in professional teaching kitchens under CIA chef-instructors, mastering core culinary techniques, knife skills, flavor construction, and baking and pastry arts. The program culminates in a celebratory banquet dinner and official Toque Ceremony.
eligibility: High school students entering grades 9-12.
cost: $3,499 (commuter) to $4,499 (residential)

name: JWU Summer Cooking Camp for Teens
summary: Johnson & Wales University offers a week-long summer culinary day camp for teenagers at its Providence campus. Led by faculty from the College of Food Innovation & Technology, students spend mornings mastering savory culinary techniques and afternoons learning baking and pastry applications. The hands-on curriculum emphasizes kitchen safety, teamwork, global flavors, and culinary creativity.
eligibility: Open to teenagers ages 13 to 17.
cost: $700 per week

name: USF Wyndham Hospitality Experience
summary: The USF Wyndham Hospitality Experience is a summer program hosted by the University of South Florida in partnership with the Wyndham Grand Clearwater Beach Hotel. High schoolers explore luxury hotel operations, guest services, catering, event planning, and culinary innovation through hands-on workshops and behind-the-scenes access. Participants gain practical skills and industry insights directly from hospitality professionals.
eligibility: Entering high school students in grades 9-12.

name: Hospitality Careers Academy
summary: The Hospitality Careers Academy is a summer program in Athens, Georgia, designed for high school students interested in hospitality management, event production, marketing, and culinary arts. Over one week, participants interact with industry executives, shadow hospitality professionals, and complete a capstone project executing a live event for hundreds of guests.
eligibility: High school students; requires application including teacher reference, short response, and virtual interview.
cost: Free to attend for accepted participants

name: Walnut Hill College High School Culinary & Pastry Arts Competitions
summary: Walnut Hill College hosts annual spring Culinary Arts and Pastry Arts Competitions for high school seniors in Philadelphia. Culinary participants execute precise cooking techniques and invent original side dishes under timed kitchen conditions, while pastry participants craft and present custom artisan cakes. Top performers earn major college scholarships toward culinary and hospitality degree programs.
eligibility: High school seniors who have applied and been admitted to Walnut Hill College.
cost: Free to enter; top winners receive up to $5,000+ scholarships

name: UC San Diego Sports Medicine Summer Academy
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies
summary: An intensive hands-on summer course where high school students explore musculoskeletal anatomy, injury prevention, acute wound care, therapeutic taping, and current trends in concussion research. Participants engage with clinical professionals, conduct a sports medicine research project, and utilize wearable technology to analyze physical performance and wellness.
eligibility: Entering 11th or 12th grade with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher
cost: $3,500 tuition

name: Health and Exercise Science Institute
summary: A week-long residential immersion program where high schoolers dive into kinesiology, biomechanics, pulmonary testing, and exercise physiology. Students participate in hands-on heart rate, blood pressure, and muscle function labs while touring university athletic facilities and interacting with sports performance experts.
eligibility: Current 9th through 12th grade high school students
cost: $3,500 tuition (overnight residential)

name: Sports Biz Careers Career Exploration Camps
summary: A free career exploration camp offered in select metropolitan markets that introduces high school students to pathways in sports marketing, analytics, media, agency, and venue management. Participants visit major athletic facilities and professional stadiums while networking with over 300 sports industry executives.
eligibility: High school students interested in learning about careers in sports business
cost: Free to attend; requires a refundable $50 deposit upon registration

name: Cleveland State University Sport Management Institute
summary: A three-day immersive workshop hosted by the Monte Ahuja College of Business where high schoolers learn about sports marketing, community relations, venue operations, and event management. Students participate in lectures from industry experts, collaborate on real-world case studies, and tour major downtown Cleveland sports venues.
eligibility: High school students interested in sport and entertainment management
cost: Paid registration fee (includes lunch daily and site tours)

name: Youth Theological Initiative (YTI) Summer Academy
org: Candler School of Theology, Emory University
summary: The YTI Summer Academy is a two-week residential program at Emory University where high school students engage in theological inquiry, spiritual discernment, and social justice exploration. Participants use seminary-level tools to study questions of faith and ethics, build intentional community, and examine how to put their commitments into action.
eligibility: Rising high school 10th, 11th, and 12th graders who are at least 15 years old by the start of the academy.
cost: Tuition and residential fees apply; financial aid and scholarships are available.

name: Saints & Scholars Summer Theology Institute
summary: Saints & Scholars is a one-week pre-college institute at Holy Cross College and the University of Notre Dame where students explore the Catholic intellectual tradition and earn college credit. Participants choose a specific track (such as music, science, media, education, or ecology) to study how Christian faith intersects with contemporary culture and career callings.
eligibility: High school students interested in theology, Catholic tradition, and faith-based leadership.
cost: $425 program fee covers college credit, classroom materials, room, and board.

name: Notre Dame Vision for High School Students
org: McGrath Institute for Church Life, University of Notre Dame
summary: Notre Dame Vision is a 5-day summer conference designed to help high schoolers recognize God's grace in their lives and explore their vocational callings. Guided by undergraduate mentors and keynote speakers, students participate in large-group sessions, small faith-sharing circles, and community prayer while experiencing campus life at Notre Dame.
eligibility: Rising high school freshmen through graduating seniors.
cost: Registration fees range from approximately $340 to $490 depending on registration timing; scholarships are available.

name: CrossRoad Summer Program
summary: CrossRoad is a 10-day academic summer institute that introduces high school juniors and seniors to the Orthodox Christian theological and spiritual tradition. Through daily worship, interactive theology lectures, community service, and peer discussion, participants learn to make major life choices grounded in faith.
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors (rising 11th and 12th graders).
cost: Need-based financial aid is available to accepted participants.

name: Interfaith Youth Group
summary: The Interfaith Youth Group brings together high school students from diverse religious and cultural backgrounds to build relationships, practice interfaith dialogue, and develop leadership skills. Members visit local places of worship, discuss core beliefs, plan community events, and participate in local service projects.
eligibility: High school students interested in interfaith dialogue, community service, and cross-cultural understanding.
cost: Free to participate.

name: Inspirit AI Scholars Program
summary: Inspirit AI Scholars is a 25-hour live online artificial intelligence bootcamp taught by Stanford and MIT alumni and graduate students. Students learn computer vision, deep learning, and natural language processing concepts, then apply them to build mentor-guided hands-on AI projects in fields like healthcare, deepfake detection, or autonomous systems.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 interested in artificial intelligence; open to domestic and international applicants.
cost: Paid tuition; need-based financial aid is available

name: Stanford AI4ALL Program
summary: Stanford AI4ALL is an intensive two-week summer program designed to introduce rising 10th graders to the fields of artificial intelligence and data science. Participants attend lectures from Stanford faculty, work in small groups on applied AI research projects, and receive mentorship from leading AI researchers.
eligibility: Current 9th-grade students (rising 10th graders) at time of application; designed to increase diversity and representation in artificial intelligence.
cost: Free / need-based financial aid available depending on program delivery mode

name: North American Computational Linguistics Open Competition (NACLO)
summary: NACLO is an annual competition where high school and middle school students solve complex linguistic and computational puzzles. Participants analyze data from unfamiliar natural and artificial languages using analytical reasoning, pattern recognition, and logic. Top performers advance to the Invitational Round and can qualify to represent the USA or Canada at the International Linguistics Olympiad.
eligibility: Open to middle and high school students in the US and Canada. No prior knowledge of linguistics or second languages is required.
cost: Free to enter

name: Summer Linguistic Institute for Youth Scholars (SLIYS)
org: The Ohio State University Department of Linguistics
summary: SLIYS is an interactive summer program introducing high schoolers to the scientific study of human language. Delivered live online by OSU faculty and researchers, students explore phonetics, syntax, morphology, and language documentation through lectures, language experimental work, and daily fieldwork sessions with native speakers of unfamiliar languages.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9–12 (including rising 9th graders).
cost: $550 tuition fee per 1-week session; need-based financial aid is available

name: Summer Youth Camp for Computational Linguistics (SYCCL)
summary: SYCCL is an intensive summer program co-hosted by Stony Brook's Department of Linguistics and the Institute for Advanced Computational Science. Participants learn how natural language processing technologies function, explore open-source software tools, and work on collaborative projects analyzing language structures and less-documented world languages.
eligibility: Middle and high school students interested in language science, computer programming, and language technology.
cost: Tuition fees apply; see official site for updated summer rates

name: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
summary: NSLI-Y provides fully funded merit-based scholarships for American high school students to study critical foreign languages including Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi, Indonesian, Korean, Persian, Russian, and Turkish. Programs run as 6-to-7-week summer immersions or full academic year abroad experiences, combining rigorous language instruction with host family stays and cultural activities.
eligibility: U.S. citizens enrolled in high school (ages 15–18 at program start) with a minimum 2.5 GPA.
cost: Fully funded scholarship covering international travel, tuition, housing, and living stipends

name: Stephen Spender Prize for Poetry in Translation
summary: The Stephen Spender Prize is an annual poetry translation competition celebrating multilingualism and creative translation. Entrants translate any published poem from any language (ancient or modern) into English and submit a short commentary reflecting on their translation choices. The competition features dedicated youth categories with publication and book prizes.
eligibility: UK and Irish citizens/residents or pupils at British schools overseas, aged 18 and under (with dedicated 14-and-under and 18-and-under categories).
cost: Free to enter

name: United Kingdom Linguistics Olympiad (UKLO)
summary: UKLO is an annual language-analysis competition where students decode unfamiliar languages using analytical and logical thinking. Questions present data from lesser-known languages worldwide as interactive puzzles, requiring contestants to deduce vocabulary rules, syntax, and writing systems without prior linguistic training.
eligibility: Primary and secondary school students enrolled in registered UK schools across multiple age-based tiers.
cost: Free to enter

name: Youth Documentary Workshop
summary: The Youth Documentary Workshop is an intensive after-school program where high school students collaborate to research, direct, shoot, and edit documentary films on social justice issues. Participants learn camera operation, interviewing techniques, and Adobe Premiere editing while earning school credit or stipends.
eligibility: NYC public high school students (with focus on Transfer, International, Consortium, and District 79 schools)
cost: Free (includes stipends and paid internship opportunities)

name: Fresh Films Weekly Filmmaking Program
summary: Fresh Films offers hands-on media production training where students create music videos, how-to clips, short documentaries, and scripted films alongside industry professionals. Participants develop skills in camera operation, lighting, audio recording, and editing while building a digital creative portfolio.
eligibility: Teens aged 13-19 interested in film, content creation, or visual storytelling; no prior experience required.
cost: Free

name: School of Doc
summary: School of Doc is a free intensive documentary filmmaking program for high school students run by the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival. Working as a crew, participants gain hands-on instruction in camera, lighting, sound design, editing, and clearance rights to produce a complete documentary film.
eligibility: Durham Public Schools high school students.
cost: Free (includes meals)

name: Summer High School Filmmakers Workshop
org: NYU Tisch School of the Arts
summary: The Tisch Summer High School Filmmakers Workshop introduces students to visual storytelling, digital video cameras, lighting, sound, and non-linear editing on Adobe Premiere Pro. Working in crews, participants direct, shoot, and edit multiple short visual projects culminating in a 3 to 4 minute film.
eligibility: High school students interested in film and digital video production.
cost: Tuition and fee required (college credit awarded)

name: National YoungArts Competition - Film
summary: YoungArts recognizes high school visual storytellers across narrative, documentary, experimental, and animation filmmaking disciplines. Winners receive financial awards, mentorship from accomplished film artists, and opportunities to showcase their work nationally.
eligibility: US citizens, permanent residents, or legally eligible high school students in grades 10–12 or ages 15–18.
cost: Application fee required (fee waivers available)

name: All American High School Film Festival
org: All American High School Film Festival
summary: The All American High School Film Festival is a global competition and festival celebrating young directors, cinematographers, and digital storytellers. Submitted films across categories like short narrative, documentary, animation, and music video are judged by industry professionals, with selected works screened in NYC.
eligibility: High school filmmakers and media arts students worldwide.
cost: Submission fee required

name: GRAMMY Camp
summary: GRAMMY Camp is a seven-day non-residential summer music program where high schoolers work directly with industry professionals and guest artists. Students choose specialized career tracks including Music Production, Audio Engineering, Songwriting, Instrumental/Vocal Performance, and Music Business, gaining hands-on recording and performance experience in professional studio settings.
eligibility: U.S. high school students in grades 9-12 with basic proficiency in their selected career track
cost: $2,000–$3,000 depending on location; need-based financial assistance available

name: YoungArts National Arts Competition - Music Discipline
summary: The YoungArts competition recognizes high school artists across Classical Music, Jazz, Voice, and Composition. Selected winners receive cash awards up to $10,000, mentorship from leading artists, eligibility for nomination as a U.S. Presidential Scholar in the Arts, and invitations to National YoungArts Week.
eligibility: U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or legally able to receive taxable income in the U.S., ages 15-18 or in grades 10-12
cost: Application fee required, with fee waivers available; cash prizes awarded up to $10,000

name: Aspire: Five-Week Music Performance Intensive
summary: A five-week immersive summer music performance program where students receive individual private lessons, participate in ensemble rehearsals, and study music theory, ear training, and improvisation with Berklee faculty. Participants earn college credit and perform in final showcase concerts.
eligibility: High school musicians ages 15+ with instrument or vocal experience
cost: Paid tuition plus optional housing and registration fees; college credit offered

name: Clive Davis Institute Summer High School Program
org: NYU Tisch School of the Arts
summary: A four-week residential program at NYU where high school sophomores and juniors earn six college credits while studying music recording, digital production, songwriting, editing, and music entrepreneurship. Students work hands-on in state-of-the-art studios guided by industry faculty.
eligibility: High school sophomores and juniors in good academic standing with a interest in music production
cost: NYU summer tuition for 6 college credits plus housing and meals

name: Stanford Jazz Workshop - Jazz Institute
summary: An intensive one-week summer jazz program hosted on the Stanford University campus for advanced high school instrumentalists and vocalists. Students work closely with master jazz musicians in small combos, study jazz theory and improvisation, and attend nightly performances at the Stanford Jazz Festival.
eligibility: Advanced jazz instrumentalists and vocalists ages 14-18; audition required
cost: $895–$2,145 per week depending on commuter or residential status; financial aid available

name: Interlochen Arts Camp - Music Programs
summary: A premiere summer arts program offering one-week to six-week intensives in Music Production & Engineering, Music Composition, Orchestral Performance, and Jazz. High schoolers receive masterclass instruction, work in digital audio technology labs, and perform live on campus.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12; audition or portfolio submission required based on discipline
cost: Tuition ranges from $2,050 for 1-week intensives to $10,350 for 6-week sessions; need and merit financial aid available

name: Juilliard Pre-College Program
summary: A comprehensive Saturday conservatory program operating throughout the academic school year for musically gifted students preparing for collegiate music study. Students receive private instrument or composition instruction, take ear training and music theory, and perform in chamber music and orchestral ensembles.
eligibility: Elementary through high school students who demonstrate exceptional musical talent and ambition; competitive live audition required
cost: Annual tuition; full and partial need-based scholarships available
